extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH/NINDS grant applications (writing the Specific Aims page)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing the one-page Specific Aims section of an NIH/NINDS research grant application, covering content, structure, emphasis, feasibility, and reviewer-facing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a research gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a research gap. Can your research move your field forward?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit the unmet need or knowledge gap your project addresses and how filling it would advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine significance and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the significance of the problem and impact. Is the work important—will progress make a difference to our understanding of neuroscience and/or human health?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why the problem matters and what difference successful completion will make to neuroscience or human health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate team experience and ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is your team experienced and able to carry out the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey investigator and collaborator qualifications that show you can complete the proposed work within the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish exploratory vs confirmatory work
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether your research questions are exploratory (hypothesis-generating) or confirmatory (hypothesis-testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confirmatory, ensure hypotheses are focused, testable, built on a solid scientific foundation, and important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of aims within grant period
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft aims to generate and/or test the hypotheses feasibly within the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design aims that are achievable in the proposed timeframe; outline approximate personnel, resources, and timeline to support feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to page/length expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually a one-page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the Specific Aims concise and within the typical one-page expectation unless guidance for the mechanism indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make aims focused and assessable
rubrics_metrics.description: The aims should be focused and easy to assess by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write aims that are clear, specific, and framed so reviewers can readily judge success; for many mechanisms, consider avoiding interdependent aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid interdependent aims (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: For many mechanisms, consider avoiding interdependent aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure aims to be as independent as possible so that failure of one aim does not doom the entire project, unless interdependence is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline experiments and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline experiments and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise sense of the major experiments and the expected outcomes so reviewers understand how aims will be accomplished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate personnel, resources, timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine approximate personnel, resources, and timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough information to support feasibility claims (who will do the work, what major resources are required, and the expected schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify appropriate funding institute and mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a potential funding institute and funding mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show fit by naming or aligning aims with an institute’s priorities or the goals of the funding mechanism where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider study section and reviewer expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider potential study sections and expertise of reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the level of background and technical detail so reviewers with the expected expertise can fairly evaluate the application; if review may be broad, include more context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess feasibility within funding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess feasibility of your proposed work within the proposed funding mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the scope, aims, and timeline match the constraints and expectations of the mechanism (budget, duration, scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Iteratively revise aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise aims as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine wording, focus, and structure through multiple drafts to improve clarity and reviewer-readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with a clear project goal sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative describing the rationale and significance of your planned research. A good way to start is with a sentence that states your project's goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a single clear sentence stating the overall objective of the project to orient reviewers immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify chosen approach vs alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases, you may want to explain why you did not take an alternative route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, briefly note and justify why you selected your approach and why alternatives are less suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: State hypothesis and link to prior/preliminary studies
rubrics_metrics.description: State your hypothesis (if relevant) and briefly describe your aims and how they build on rigorous prior and preliminary studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit hypotheses and show how they arise from prior literature or preliminary data to demonstrate rationale and preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide field status and project fit for broad review
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is likely your application will be reviewed by a study section with broad expertise, summarize the status of research in your field and explain how your project fits in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer accessible context so non-specialist reviewers can appreciate the project's significance and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: State planned technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: State the technologies they plan to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List key techniques or technologies to give reviewers a sense of approach and feasibility; avoid excessive technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note investigator and collaborator expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Note their expertise to do a specific task or that of collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant skills and prior achievements that demonstrate the team can execute the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe past accomplishments related to the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe past accomplishments related to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly cite notable prior work from the team that supports their capability to complete the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe preliminary studies and recent relevant findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe preliminary studies and new and highly relevant findings in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary data and recent literature to strengthen the rationale and feasibility of the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain relevant biology
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain their area's biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide necessary biological context that helps reviewers understand the mechanistic basis for hypotheses and experimental design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show how aims relate to one another
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how the aims relate to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain logical connections among aims (complementary, sequential, or independent) to present a coherent project narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use typographic emphasis strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bold or italics to emphasize items they want to bring to the reviewers' attention, such as the hypothesis or rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply emphasis sparingly to draw reviewer attention to the most important elements (hypothesis, major outcomes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor emphasis for career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on your situation, decide which items are important for you. For example, an Early-Stage Investigator may want to highlight preliminary data and qualifications to do the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust which elements you emphasize based on career stage, reviewer expectations, and the review context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format aims clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: After the narrative, enter your aims as stand-alone headers, run-on headers, or bullet points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a clear, scannable format (headers or bullets) so reviewers can quickly see each aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use strong, action-oriented verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: State your plans using strong verbs like identify, define, quantify, establish, determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin aim statements with decisive verbs to convey clear, testable objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise aim length
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe each aim in one to three sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise yet specific: one to three sentences per aim is recommended to convey scope and approach without overloading the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bullets to refine objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider adding bullets under each aim to refine your objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bullets can clarify sub-objectives, key experiments, or milestones under each aim while keeping the primary aim statement succinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe expected outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe expected outcomes for each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what results you anticipate and how they will address the hypotheses or research gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain data interpretation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how you plan to interpret data from the aim’s efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the criteria or analyses you will use to judge success and interpret findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address potential pitfalls and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how to address potential pitfalls with contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge major risks and present realistic alternative approaches or mitigations to reassure reviewers of project robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional closing paragraph to reinforce significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some people add a closing paragraph, emphasizing the significance of the work, their collaborators, or whatever else they want to focus reviewers' attention on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a brief closing to re-emphasize impact, team strengths, or translational potential as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek colleague review for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: It can be useful to have a colleague review your aims for clarity (particularly a colleague outside your field or a colleague with NIH funding or NIH study section experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get feedback from both domain outsiders (for readability) and experienced NIH investigators/reviewers (for fit and competitiveness).
